To be honest, you don't need to know much more than the basics. The biggest influences on my worldview were probably:

  • The Copenhagen Interpretation of QM - that all unmeasured aspects of reality exist in a superposition and only collapse to a particular state when observed (think Schrödinger's Cat).
  • The probabilistic nature of reality (think Double Slit Experiment).
  • The Uncertainty Principle - the fact that there's a fundamental limit to how precisely we can measure our world.
  • The Many Worlds Interpretation of QM - the potential for parallel timelines.

Note that those are vastly simplified. The impact wasn't so much the raw knowledge of these, rather when I started to integrate them into my understandings of other phenomena and considering their philosophical implications.
